critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_memory: Make the identity tracking connection explicit for this exchange: the red-associated cover at approximately front pixel (145,110) in E87 moves through (131,120) in E104 to the lower-left cover near (125,125) in E120, not the upper-left cover near (124,99). Its updated location is approximately [0.107,-0.009]. The green-associated cover remains the lower-right cover; localize its top-face center rather than its silhouette center, giving approximately [0.119,0.183].

Specify how to localize a container elevated during an exchange, not only one lifted by the gripper. At E146 the green-associated container is still moving; applying the resting-cover height produced [0.03, 0.103] rather than the recorded [0.017, 0.11]. The instruction needs an observable rule for estimating its current elevation and projecting its central axis during this motion, or a rule to retain the last reliable location when that elevation cannot be resolved.

Make explicit that after the first pickup, only the remaining green-target container must qualify tracking_frame. At E380 that container is unambiguously localizable in the front image at the carried green location, so advance tracking_frame to E380 even though the robot occludes other containers. Do not require visibility of already-completed targets or all containers.

The surface height used for localization needs clarification. At E108 I tracked the red-associated container correctly but projecting its top-face center at the instructed approximate z=0.06 m gave [0.120,-0.036], not the recorded [0.131,-0.037]. Specify the actual top-face height and consistent center landmark used by the annotator prompt; millimetre rounding cannot resolve this projection discrepancy.

Clarify that preserving stationary coordinates does not mean ignoring residual container motion during button approaches. Here the red-associated frontmost cover shifts between E108/E109 and E125 and then settles by E135; update its x coordinate from 0.131 to 0.143, retaining y=-0.037 and the unchanged green-target location, rather than treating this shift as estimation jitter.

At E114, identify the tracked blue-cube cover's horizontal top-face center near front-image pixel (190, 96), rather than the lower apparent body center near (190, 99). Projecting that top-face center at z≈0.06 gives approximately [-0.007, 0.215]. The top-face localization rule needed this more explicit distinction; the identity tracking itself was correct.

The target correspondence was available, but the geometric localization rule did not settle the center of the rotated lower-right cover at E145. It should specify estimating the full top-face center from its opposing edges, rather than the center of a bright visible patch, and the surface height to use for that projection. This must explain the recorded [0.111, 0.211] versus my [0.116, 0.196]; no additional hidden-color history was missing.

The coordinate-estimation convention needs to be more precise. I tracked the blue-associated cover to the lower-right cover correctly, but estimated its center as [0.116, 0.121] rather than [0.123, 0.133]. Specify the exact visual reference point and projection height used by the annotator prompt; 'horizontal top-face center' at 'approximately z=0.06 m' does not settle this numerical difference. No additional identity memory is needed.

annotator_prompt.name: target_locations
annotator_prompt.description: During button pressing and retraction, requested covers exchanged positions and sometimes continued moving after the hand reached its waypoint. The policy generally chose the correct button waypoint, but its stored target positions sometimes followed the wrong exchange branch or differed from the annotation by more than 1 cm. Some annotations also required an elevation estimate that the available images did not establish. This breaks PREDICTABILITY. Retain the ordered list of requested targets' central-axis world [x,y] coordinates, but use a reproducible geometric landmark: reconstruct the entire horizontal top square from its opposing outer edges and use its diagonal intersection, not the center of a bright patch, inset panel, visible side, or silhouette. Use approximately z=0.06 m only for a resting cover. For a cover elevated during an exchange, require visible geometric evidence for its elevation, such as a resolvable known-size top square or simultaneous calibrated views; otherwise retain the last reliably localized coordinate until localization becomes possible. Do not fill an intermediate coordinate using later frames or an unobservable assumed height. Recheck existing intermediate annotations under this convention rather than treating their millimetre-rounded numbers as ground truth. Follow identity through every available intermediate frame, including changes in image ranking; update after residual translation even during an unrelated button approach. Preserve coordinates only when the images support stationarity. An example ordered value is [[0.107, -0.009], [-0.027, 0.152]]. Keep the existing world-coordinate comparison tolerance.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: target_locations
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: During exchanges triggered while the hand was pressing or retracting from buttons, the button action was usually correct but the target memory could follow the wrong cover or localize the right cover from an inconsistent landmark. This breaks PREDICTABILITY, not a demonstrated need for more hidden-color fields. Keep the fixed requested-order list of central-axis [x,y] coordinates. Establish correspondence from the incoming locations and retained frame, then trace each target through every chronological frame before computing its endpoint coordinate. In particular, continue a moving cover's trajectory when it passes below another cover; do not reconnect it to the cover occupying its former upper or lower slot. Reconstruct the full horizontal top square using opposing outer edges and their corners; its center is the intersection of the diagonals. Do not use a bright patch, inset panel, side face, or overall body center. Project that center at approximately z=0.06 m only when the cover is resting. During an airborne exchange, estimate elevation only if the known-size face geometry or available calibrated views actually resolve it; if not, carry the last reliable coordinate rather than projecting onto the resting plane or guessing a correction. Update once reliable geometry becomes visible again. Compare successive front frames for residual translation: reaching a button waypoint does not imply that covers have settled. Preserve a coordinate only when the observed cover is stationary, not merely because its identity is unchanged. For example, a red target may finish at [0.107, -0.009] while the green target continues moving. Write the resulting list to millimetre resolution without claiming that measurement accuracy.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: tracking_frame
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: After the first of two requested pickups had been released and the empty hand withdrawn, the policy correctly approached the remaining target but retained an older tracking frame because other covers were occluded. The annotation advanced to the current frame. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure in applying the existing still-needed qualification. Explicitly define still-needed targets as the requested entries at indices greater than or equal to the observed updated pickups_completed count. Use that updated count when evaluating frame eligibility in the same cycle. Already successfully lifted targets do not need to be visible, even if they have been covered again. Write the latest shown frame in which every remaining target has unambiguous identity and localization from the views actually available for that frame. Retain the previous label if none qualifies. For example, after the first pickup, a current label such as E380 qualifies when the second target alone is clearly localized, regardless of occlusion of the first target or distractors. This clarifies the existing annotator prompt rather than changing which frames it should select.

proposal.refused: Do not add episode-specific pixel paths, final coordinates, or color-to-slot shortcuts. The reported wrong exchange branch is addressed by chronological correspondence, not by memorizing a particular red-cover path. Do not invent an exact top height or an elevation correction solely to reproduce annotated numbers: the supplied evidence does not establish such a constant, and future-only reconstruction would make the runtime memory unpredictable. Instead, apply the same observable landmark and reliability convention to annotation and policy. Do not widen the 1 cm coordinate tolerance to hide these discrepancies. The reports about already-completed targets being irrelevant to tracking-frame eligibility and about residual motion do not justify new memory fields; they clarify existing rules. Failures that supplied no missing-information account do not establish an additional action-rule defect. The button waypoints were generally consistent with the intended milestone, and the supplied evidence does not justify replacing the button localization or interaction-state rules. No action-instruction change is proposed.

Keep this requested order fixed. Match each descending cover to the cube underneath. Reconstruct the full horizontal top square from opposing outer edges and corners, and use the intersection of its diagonals as the central-axis landmark. Do not use a bright patch, inset panel, side face, or silhouette centroid. Project that landmark at approximately z=0.06 m only when the cover is resting; do not project its elevated top onto the table plane. For an elevated cover, estimate elevation only when resolvable known-size face geometry or available simultaneous calibrated views actually establish it. Otherwise carry the last reliably localized coordinate rather than projecting onto the resting plane or guessing an elevation correction. Update when reliable geometry becomes visible again. Using the carried locations and tracking_frame to establish initial correspondence, trace each specific container through every available chronological frame before computing its endpoint coordinate. A carried coordinate may predate unresolved airborne motion; use the visual trajectory rather than treating that coordinate as a new spatial identity assignment. At crossings, use continuous motion through intermediate frames, allowing horizontal and vertical image ranking to change; do not transfer identity by nearest previous position, initial slot, or final spatial order alone. Compare successive front frames for residual translation, including during unrelated button motions: reaching a hand waypoint does not imply that covers have settled. Update coordinates after reliably localized translation, including movement during grasping or release. Preserve coordinates when images support stationarity rather than introducing estimation jitter. When localization is unreliable or temporarily occluded, carry the last reliable location without assuming the cover is stationary. Keep tracking later requested targets during button pressing and earlier pickups; use a newly exposed cube to confirm correspondence. Write coordinates to millimetre resolution without implying millimetre measurement accuracy. e.g. [[0.02, -0.18], [0.03, 0.13]]

Before covering, use the central axes of the corresponding visible cubes. At covering, associate each cube with the container descending over it. Reconstruct the full horizontal top square from its opposing outer edges and corners; use the intersection of its diagonals as the central-axis landmark, not a bright patch, inset panel, side face, or silhouette centroid. Project this landmark at approximately z=0.06 m only for a resting container. For an elevated container, use an elevation estimate only when the images available through this cycle resolve it, for example from resolvable known-size face geometry or simultaneous calibrated views. Otherwise retain the last reliably localized coordinate until reliable geometry becomes visible. Do not derive intermediate coordinates from later cycles or an assumed airborne height. Recheck intermediate annotations using this same landmark and observability convention. Follow each container continuously through every shuffle, allowing its horizontal and vertical image ranking to change at crossings; neither its initial slot nor nearest position alone establishes identity. Check correspondence through successive frames across the episode and correct an erroneous association at its first occurrence and throughout its subsequent values, rather than switching identities at the endpoint. Trace identity through every available chronological frame before localizing the endpoint. Update coordinates after reliably localized translation, including residual exchange motion during button approaches and movement during grasping or release. Reaching a hand waypoint does not establish that containers have settled. Preserve the carried coordinate when images support stationarity; when localization is unreliable or temporarily occluded, retain the last reliable estimate without treating that retention as evidence of stationarity. Write coordinates to millimetre resolution without implying millimetre measurement accuracy. Track only requested targets, including the second target while manipulating the first. Do not assign an unseen color from the final arrangement alone. e.g. [[0.02, -0.18], [0.03, 0.13]]

fields.name: tracking_frame
fields.description: First incorporate any successful lift observed this cycle into pickups_completed. Still-needed targets are entries at zero-based indices greater than or equal to that updated count. Write the latest shown label for which every such remaining target container, or initially uncovered target cube, can be localized unambiguously from the available front and wrist views together. Already successfully lifted targets and distractors need not be visible, even if a completed target has been covered again. The current wrist image may qualify its shared current-frame label; do not assume a wrist image is available for every intermediate motion frame. Partial occlusion is permissible if the available images establish the target centers and correspondence unambiguously. If none qualifies, carry the previous label. At the first cycle write E0. Use this retained keyframe with target_locations to establish identities at the beginning of the next clip. e.g. "E114"
fields.annotation: Latest shown frame label at which all still-needed target containers, or their initially uncovered cubes, can be localized unambiguously using the available front image and, when available for that label, wrist image together. Still-needed targets are entries at zero-based indices greater than or equal to pickups_completed after incorporating the successful lifts observed in this cycle. Use this updated count when evaluating frame eligibility. Already successfully lifted targets and distractors need not be visible, even if a completed target has been covered again. Partial occlusion is permissible when the target centers and correspondence remain unambiguous. Do not assume wrist images exist for intermediate motion frames. Retain the preceding value if no qualifying frame appears in the cycle. This keyframe anchors correspondence between the stored target locations and the next motion clip. Initialize with E0. e.g. "E114"

fields.name: interaction_state
fields.description: Initialize start. Update from observed outcomes and the incoming milestone, not from the action you are about to choose. A completed approach above the robot-left button gives left_hover; its subsequent short close-only motion gives left_ready; descent to button contact gives left_pressed; upward withdrawal gives left_retracted. Apply the analogous right_hover, right_ready, right_pressed, right_retracted milestones at the robot-right button. In particular, arrival with already-closed fingers is still right_hover, not right_ready: the separate short closing action must be observed. Opening after right_retracted gives buttons_finished. Arrival above the next requested container at about 0.20 m gives target_hover; descending and closing around it near 0.063 m gives target_grasped; lifting it clear near 0.20 m gives target_lifted; lowering and opening near 0.07 m gives target_released; withdrawing the empty hand near 0.15 m gives target_cleared. A subsequent approach to the next target returns to target_hover. Retain the incoming state if the expected outcome has not occurred or no control steps executed. e.g. "right_ready"
fields.annotation: Observed interaction milestone, initially start. Button milestones are left_hover, left_ready, left_pressed, left_retracted, right_hover, right_ready, right_pressed, right_retracted, buttons_finished. Hover means the initial approach to that button has finished; ready means the subsequent short closing action has finished, even if the fingers were already closed on arrival. Pressed means the closed hand has descended into button contact; retracted means it has subsequently risen to approximately 0.15 m. buttons_finished means the hand has subsequently opened above the right button. Container milestones are target_hover, target_grasped, target_lifted, target_released, target_cleared. They respectively mean arrival at the selected container's 0.20 m approach, closure around it near 0.063 m, successful lift near 0.20 m, lowering and opening near 0.07 m, and empty-hand withdrawal near 0.15 m. Change only when the corresponding motion outcome is observed, never when its waypoint is selected. e.g. "right_ready"

fields.name: pickups_completed
fields.description: Initialize zero. Increment only when the incoming state is target_grasped and the current clip shows the held requested container successfully raised clear to about 0.20 m, ordinarily revealing its colored cube. Carry the count unchanged in every other situation, including further views of that same held container. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of requested containers successfully lifted in instruction order. Initialize to zero. Increment once when a newly grasped requested container is visibly raised off the table to approximately 0.20 m, exposing its cube. Do not increment for grasp closure, release, withdrawal, or repeated observations of the same lift. e.g. 1

texts.action:
Use the incoming memory together with outcomes visible this cycle to determine the current milestone; write those observations for the next cycle. Begin by locating both buttons and all requested colored cubes. Robot-left is larger world y, appearing on the right of the front image. Estimate geometry with the calibrated cameras, intersecting image rays with the appropriate object surface height rather than treating elevated tops as table points. Use wrist imagery to refine alignment. Do not reuse episode-specific coordinates.

Button rules: Independently localize each button using the center of its circular press surface, intersecting its calibrated image ray with approximately z=0.025 m. Do not use the square base centroid, a table-plane projection, the other button's x coordinate, or the achieved TCP position as its center. Prefer the current calibrated wrist view when the circle is visible. At hover and ready milestones, recompute the button center and command its x,y even if the preceding approach was accepted as complete or the closing action produced little motion. Hover tolerance establishes the milestone, not exact lateral alignment. All references below to the button center mean this visually localized center. From start, approach the robot-left button center at z=0.15 m, orientation [-3.1416,0,0], gripper open. At left_hover, command closure above the same center at z=0.15. At left_ready, descend over that center to commanded z=0.0075, closed. Actual contact may stop the TCP near z=0.024; this counts as contact, not a reason to press deeper. At left_pressed, retract over the localized left-button center to z=0.15 closed. At left_retracted, approach the robot-right button center at z=0.15 with an open command. At right_hover, perform the separate short closing action above the button even when the reported fingers are already closed. At right_ready, descend to z=0.0075 closed. At right_pressed, retract over the localized right-button center to z=0.15 closed. At right_retracted, open above the same button. Continue observing and tracking container exchanges throughout all these motions. Neither a return to the original spatial arrangement nor an unchanged shell appearance resets its hidden color association.

Container rules: After buttons_finished, select target_locations[pickups_completed]. At target_cleared, select that same indexed next uncompleted target. Approach its current center at z=0.20, open, pointing straight down. Choose yaw from its visible square edges so the fingers grasp opposing sides; use an equivalent square-symmetry orientation near zero where possible. If an expected motion did not execute, retain memory milestones and retry with a reachable, nonidentical waypoint. Do not guess a hidden color from its original slot, and do not wait without a specific visibility or settling purpose.
